main_text.p: Γράφω, scribo, sculpo: Nempe, quòd ut sculpebant stylo, ita & (in pugi-laribus scil.) olim scribebant aut eo-dem, aut simillimo. Anglis, to grave; sculpere: olim (ne quis ex Gal. graver mutuatum fùspicetùr:) grafen. grafe-num anliengffum beoza : sculptilibus fuis, Pfal.LXXVIII. 58. Hinc etiam for-taffe & alterùm synonymum, to carve, ? ?.leviter tranfpofito, ut in χαράσσω, χάρ-ᾳ, &c. & γ. in κ. (quod non rarum) mutato. Aliam tamen originem non minùs probabilem paulò poft ex verbo ἐξυκεάς excuIpturi fumus, de quâ le-ctoris (ut in dubiis) efto judicium.
Γραφὴ, scriptura, sculptura, a grave: ut proprie de monumento pro more inscripto vel infculpto, dictum fuerit.
main_text.head: Δ
main_text.p: Ἀϊς, Ἀλίμ, convivium, bailtles. Est igitur, a bailtle man: proprie, cu-pediarum, & scitamentorum fe-ctator, liguritor. Gallice, un friand. Est tamen alloquin etiam λίβαξ, catillo, liguri-tor: & λιβάς, substantivum: Item & λιβάς, ejusdem significationis ver-bum:

page.notes: Several words in the Greek and in the Old English/Germanic glosses are uncertain and are not reliably transcribed; the Greek forms are approximate. The marginal decoration at top right is not text. The catchword and signature are absent. Greek letters and black-letter words (bailtles, cu-pediarum) are reproduced as best read.
